utterances.text: I said specifically that I was in charge of Urosevac, Stimlje, and Lipjan. Lipjan belongs to the Secretariat of the Interior of Pristina. Second point: It is not true that he was from Djeneral Jankovic, taken via Urosevac to Stimlje and then from Stimlje to Urosevac and I wasn't able to follow the whole route that you set out. Thirdly, it is not true and correct, and I say that with full responsibility, that he came -- a moment ago, you said a moment ago that he was brought to Stimlje --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How do you know --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- from Djeneral Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How do you know he didn't take that route? I thought you just sat behind your desk, waiting for people to arrive? How do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. A moment ago you said that when he was on his way he was stopped on the road towards Djeneral Jankovic and that from Djeneral Jankovic they took him to the police station in Stimlje and from Stimlje to the Secretariat of the Interior of Urosevac. And I know about that from Djeneral Jankovic to Urosevac via Urosevac you go to Stimlje or you take the byroad across Lipjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have translations down to paragraph 14, but I need to ask, if it's a 43 minutes past rise, I need to ask the witness some other questions on another topic to make use of his time if he's willing to help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I ask the court deputy, is the Limaj case here this afternoon? There is another case this afternoon. So 1.43.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, we've heard from Danica Marinkovic, who did not investigate or conduct an investigation into the facts of this case. We've heard from Obrad Stevanovic who was not able to conduct an investigation into this case, and you are the policeman from the Racak area. Do you have experience in your 20 years or so in the police of inquiring into crimes on your territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do have experience, a great deal of experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Have you reviewed at any stage any or many of the documents that deal with the Racak event?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean my documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Not just your documents, other documents. Reports of what happened as well as your statements saying that people were members of the KLA. Have you looked at the other documents ever?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked at my statements personally, and my statements, my notes, my information notes, I saw through the documents that there were a number of statements from the state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Statements of what kind; reports or witness statements?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Witness statements -- no. Statements from individuals who were interviewed by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But they aren't available to us today; is that right? It's something different?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the question you asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You see, we haven't had in this court, for example, a statement produced by the local authorities or by the Belgrade authorities or any other authorities from the Serb side explaining what happened in Racak. We've got a lot of bits and pieces of documents, but we haven't got a statement giving an overall account from somebody who was involved. Do you find that surprising, as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say. Probably the person who was on the spot should have written a report about the event that took place in Racak. I mean, the person in charge of the action or someone designated by him. I don't know whether such a statement exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's Goran Radosavljevic, isn't it? He was in charge. You know that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I don't know whether he was in charge or not. I'm just not aware of it. I don't know. There's no reason why I should hide anything like that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You see --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- if I knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- because as we haven't had anybody who's produced an analysis, if I were to give you as many documents as we've got in Serbian -- there are some of them in English but I would only ask you to look at the Serbian ones overnight, would you be prepared to look at those documents in order that we can save time in asking you questions about what the documents would show to a local policeman versed in the practices of the local police? Would you help us do that, Mr. Jasovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean today for tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to have a rest after these proceedings, after the trial. I'd be happy to help you, but not perhaps for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's only a question -- how big is the file, Ms. Dicklich? It's not a very big volume of material because we haven't been provided with a great deal, and half of this is in English so I wouldn't be asking you to look at the English, but if you would help us. It's a chronological compilation that we've been able to put together of what has been said or written by Serbs, authorities of one kind or another, about the Racak event. Would you be prepared to look at that for us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know whether I could do that today. I'd like to take a look at it, but whether I'll be able to get through that today I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the position, as the Court knows, is that there has been no single comprehensive document produced, and we have done our best drawing on all sources and in an entirely non-selective way to put a chronological collection together of the documents, and I would like to ask some questions about that. If the witness and the Chamber were disposed to read the material overnight, the questioning would take less time. If that's not possible, more time will be consumed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The witness does not appear disposed -- to be disposed to reading it overnight. He's not certain whether he could get through that material tonight.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, I've done my best, but can I ask him one or two more questions just so that we know what his position on Racak is -- sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before, could I ask one question? Mr. Jasovic, what position did Goran Radosavljevic hold?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be quite honest and frank, I really can't explain what work post and what position he held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He wasn't an assistant minister, so I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Tell us in a sentence, Mr. Jasovic, what happened at Racak.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the 15th of January, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a conflict between the Albanian KLA terrorists and members of the police, the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And who attacked whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who attacked who. Well, certainly the members of the KLA opened fire on members of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And then? You see, you've spoken to so many witnesses who you tell us have told you the full truth about everything, it's impossible that you don't have some understanding of events. So tell us what happened next.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know specifically what happened next on the spot. I can tell you -- I could tell you had I been there on the spot. Then I could explain the details of it to you. But as I said previously, all I do know is there was a KLA substaff. I know that there were bunkers, trenches and communicating trenches. I know that from the direction of Racak and surrounding villages a large number of terrorist attacks were launched.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I hate to stop you midstream. Experience is when we stop at 1.45, the next case begins ten to 15 minutes late.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You will have to take this up tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow, 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ... to set out a number of topics.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused repeat what he said. The microphone wasn't on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Start again, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, for the record, for the transcript, I would like -- today's record, I'd just like to enumerate a number of topics which Mr. Nice launched in his cross-examination, dealt with in his cross-examination of General Stevanovic and for which you interrupted me and did not allow me to ask General Stevanovic any questions about. You will recall, I'm sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Not now, Mr. Milosevic. If you wish to take up that matter, I'll consider it tomorrow morning at 9.00. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 16th day of June, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
